isinstance(3.0, int) is False in Python, so _int_or_zero(3.0) returns 0 instead of 3. Lines 309-310 use this helper for run_count and cell_terminal_count from CLI JSON output. If the API ever returns a numeric float (e.g. from a JSON encoder that emits 3.0), the value is silently discarded. The function accepts 'object' but its behavior on floats is neither documented nor guarded.

header_status_text (line 1023) builds 'Finalize {cov.percent}% {bar} {cov.terminal}/{cov.total}' where 'Finalize' is a hardcoded label prefix. The TUI counterpart header_status_tui_lines (line 1138) omits this prefix, showing just '{cov.percent}% {bar} {cov.terminal}/{cov.total}'. The text-mode prefix makes the coverage count read as a finalization percentage rather than a review coverage metric.

ProgressMetrics.incomplete (positional arg 5) and ProgressMetrics.pending (positional arg 6) are both set to the same pending variable at lines 594-595. The fields have different semantic contracts: incomplete should count all non-complete cells while pending should count only 'pending'-state cells. Adding a new incomplete state would silently fail to update pending, causing them to diverge without detection.
